purpose: Capability-first router for video requests. Determine the production capability the piece needs, probe that the harness can produce it, record the visual language in an art-direction contract, approve an e00 styleboard, then load only the minimum skills for that capability set.

rules.capabilityGapPolicy: A missing capability is a blocker or an explicitly approved downgrade. Never silently replace the shot with cards and text.
rules.laneMeaning: A lane names a production capability set, not an aesthetic. The visual language comes from art-direction.md.
rules.startingSkillSet: Start with the minimum useful set: one preproduction, one or two visual, one audio, one render/QA. Add another skill only when the task requires it; never load the whole catalog.
rules.companionSelection: Lane skills are candidates with conditions. Load only available skills whose condition holds; omit planned ones and note them as follow-ups.
rules.stylePresetPolicy: A named aesthetic preset is opt-in. kanagawa-html contributes its tokens, fonts, ambient blur, particles and chart palette only when art-direction.md selects the Gentleman Kanagawa aesthetic; otherwise it is loaded in craft-only mode.

craftOnlySkill.usableWhen: the declared aesthetic is not Gentleman Kanagawa

rules.effectBudget: No effect layer by default. Add shader, pixel or 3D effects only when art-direction.md names them and they survive legibility and the delivery renderer.
rules.organizingPrinciple: No two consecutive shots share the same layout skeleton unless art-direction.md names the repetition as a deliberate motif.

productionCapabilities.code-2d: HTML/CSS/SVG/canvas composition rendered deterministically by HyperFrames or the frame renderer.
productionCapabilities.vector-diagram: Exact geometry, connectors, labels and data diagrams drawn in code.
productionCapabilities.kinetic-type: Type-led motion where the words are the subject.
productionCapabilities.ui-mock: A product interface reproduced or staged in code, never faked with generated raster.
productionCapabilities.progressive-draw: Stroke-by-stroke drawing or reveal driven by the timeline.
productionCapabilities.sprite-animation: Sprite sheets or per-frame pixel animation with nearest-neighbor scaling.
productionCapabilities.pixel-art: A limited palette and pixel grid as the primary visual language.
productionCapabilities.character-rig: Named, separable character parts with pivots, z-order and pose/expression control.
productionCapabilities.raster-composite: Generated or painted raster layers composited under code elements.
productionCapabilities.raster-generation: Local or approved image generation for characters, textures or stills.
productionCapabilities.i2v: Image-to-video or generated motion clips for narrative shots.
productionCapabilities.3d-render: A deterministic 3D scene rendered frame by frame.
productionCapabilities.camera-3d: Programmatic camera moves with depth and perspective.
productionCapabilities.depth-composite: Layered 2.5D planes with parallax and depth of field.
productionCapabilities.shader-fx: Deterministic GLSL or post-process effects: grain, CRT, VHS, dither, distortion.
productionCapabilities.footage-montage: Licensed or generated footage edited into a sequence.
productionCapabilities.interview-edit: Talking-head and B-roll editing with clear attribution.
productionCapabilities.sound-design: SFX and ambience layered under voice and music.
productionCapabilities.voice: Narration generated locally or through an approved service.
productionCapabilities.music: A composed or generated score with a declared tempo and key.

director-craft.note: The art-direction contract in video-production covers shot language until this ships.

a subject recurs across shots
the art direction names a deterministic effect

generated footage or stills are part of the shot
the art direction names a deterministic effect
the same subject, set or prop recurs

generated sprite sheets are approved
generated stills or footage are approved

icons are part of the type system

a subject or location recurs

the product UI or a presenter recurs
the art direction names a deterministic effect

avoid: forcing a lane when the brief does not match any listed lane
falling back to the previous project's look

styleBrief.questionMode: one grouped question by default; ask again only if the answer would change the outcome

axes.question: Palette, typography, and motion rhythm?
axes.default: from art-direction.md plus one reference; never the previous project

axes.question: Voice, music, and SFX?
axes.default: local voice + local music, no paid service without approval

rules: Infer a candidate lane and its capabilities first; ask only what changes the outcome.
Probe every required capability before promising the lane.
Offer a recommended default and one or two alternatives, not an open questionnaire.
Accept 'surprise me' and state the chosen lane with a one-line rationale.
Record the asset policy per project with a reason; never inherit a ban.
Generate e00 with the real hero shot, palette, typography in scene, texture, and a 5-second audio preview.
Do not render the full sequence before e00 approval; idu-pi video render enforces it.
After a change, update only the affected decisions and regenerate e00.
